WORKLOG - task 0 of protection_claims_desk (Northbeam ShieldCare). Kept up to date from the first design decision; every figure below was produced by the runnable harness recorded in section 11 and re-checked by the gates in section 13.
1. STEP 0 DRAW (by code, before any tree or computation was designed)
   .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/protection_claims_desk --tasks 2
   {"task": 0, "key": "consumer_electronics_retailer/protection_claims_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 5, 5]}
   {"task": 1, "key": "consumer_electronics_retailer/protection_claims_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 6, 4]}
   Task 0 therefore has three prerequisite problems and four computations carrying 4, 5, 5 and 5 factors. The count of 4 went to the late fee (the shortest computation: one fee, one count of periods, one rate, one write-off); the three 5s went to the settlement, the repair payout and the spoilage allowance.
2. WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST
   The caller asks for one thing only - the food she lost out of the freezer. Nothing she says names the three problems that stand between that request and a correct terminal state, and no tool refuses while they are unresolved. To land the right four numbers the agent has to read the published rules, see from the records that the ceiling on the allowance is not the plan's 350.00 spoilage cover but the cover left after an approved cost that has never been paid, see that the payout itself is held while the premium period containing the incident day stands unpaid, and see that the arrears the customer must clear carries a fee for the periods past grace that was never billed. Each of the four figures is then a multi-factor calculation over reconciled history (eleven instalment entries, three claims, four payouts, three deductible pairs, a repairer's ledger on two different jobs) with cross-product reads into the Circle membership and the TechWorks service ledger. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling ledgers and arithmetic; the tool set is four tools and each problem has exactly one, so nothing here is a guess between similar tools.
3. SCOPE: OCCUPIED, CLAIMED, RESERVED
   Nothing was occupied before this task (task 0 is first). This task claims four extended policies and four task tools: protection_ext_premium_late_fee_scale / bill_premium_late_fee_5ae6a6af (a premium charge of the late-fee kind), protection_ext_premium_arrears_settlement / settle_premium_arrears_c5640f60 (a premium payment, owner user), protection_ext_claim_repair_settlement / book_claim_payout_542e239c (a claim payout in the form the decision set) and protection_ext_spoilage_allowance / book_spoilage_allowance_79e3e314 (a claim payout of the spoilage-allowance kind). Reserved for task 1, and untouched here: the claim deductible charged (protection_deductible_charge), the customer's own settlement of that deductible (protection_deductible_payment), the instalment billed for a period now running (a premium charge of the instalment kind) and the premium refund on a cancellation (protection_premium_refund). The two tasks share no policy, no tool and no (target_tool, computes) pair, and the four base event subjects they write are disjoint apart from protection_premium_charge, which is split by billing subtype into two different tools as the charter contract allows.
4. THE PROBLEM-TREE CARD
   Root: protection_ext_spoilage_allowance (the allowance for the spoiled food), the only thing the caller asks for. A single chain of four problems, three of them prerequisites:
     protection_ext_premium_late_fee_scale -> protection_ext_premium_arrears_settlement -> protection_ext_claim_repair_settlement -> protection_ext_spoilage_allowance
   Edge 1 (allowance <- payout), kind value_input, gate allowance_ceiling, form state.
     Prerequisite sentence (in the allowance policy's own rule): 'The allowance for spoiled food is worked out only after every cost the claim has already been approved for stands booked as paid against the plan's cover.' Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is 'only after'; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state - an approved cost standing booked as paid against the plan's cover - and names no action and no performer; (3) it carries no tool name, no policy id and no code token; (4) its strength is 'only after' and its scope is every approved cost of that claim, exactly the edge's condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: book_claim_payout_542e239c is the only tool that books a payout for a cost a decision approved (the allowance tool books an allowance for spoiled food, which is not a cost the claim was approved for). Derivation a reader performs: the sentence says the allowance waits on the approved cost standing paid; the records show a decision of 2026-09-08 approving a repair on SC-2026-88413 and no payout entry against that reference; the repair-settlement policy's own rule says what the plan pays on an approved claim and that booking it draws the amount from the cover; therefore the resolving action is to settle the approved cost first. Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: the newest payout on the plan is the April allowance of 2026-04-18 and coverage_remaining stands at 1470.00, untouched by the August approval.
   Edge 2 (payout <- settlement), kind state_gate, gate protection_plans.premium_outstanding, form state.
     Prerequisite sentence: 'The amount the plan pays on the claim is released only once no premium period covering the day the failure happened stands unpaid on the plan.' Four-point test: (1) 'only once'; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state, a premium period standing unpaid on the plan; (3) no tool, id or code token; (4) the strength is 'only once' and the scope is the period containing the incident day, neither wider nor narrower than the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: settle_premium_arrears_c5640f60 is the only tool that lowers what stands unpaid (the late-fee tool raises it). Derivation: the sentence says the release waits on that period being settled; the records show the failure on 2026-08-30 inside the period 2026-08-08 to 2026-09-07, that instalment billed and the last payment applied to the period beginning 2026-05-08; the settlement policy's own rule says what the customer settles and that it is applied from the oldest unpaid period; therefore the arrears must be settled first, and by the customer in person. Seed evidence: the four instalment entries from 2026-06-08 to 2026-09-08 with no payment against them.
   Edge 3 (settlement <- late fee), kind value_input, gate fees_taken, form state.
     Prerequisite sentence: 'The amount the customer settles is fixed only after every fee owed for a period that has run past grace stands billed on the plan.' Four-point test: (1) 'only after'; (2) a record-visible state, a fee standing billed on the plan; (3) no tool, id or code token; (4) 'only after ... every fee owed' matches the condition exactly. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings it about: bill_premium_late_fee_5ae6a6af. Derivation: the sentence says the settlement waits on the fee standing billed; the records carry eleven premium charges, every one of the monthly instalment kind, and grace on the period beginning 2026-06-08 ran out on 2026-07-08; the late-fee policy's own rule says what fee is owed once grace has run; therefore the fee must be billed first. Seed evidence: premium_kind on every charge row is monthly_instalment.
   Topological order: late fee, settlement, payout, allowance - the order of the gold writes at actions 9, 11, 13 and 15. There are no parallel edges, so nothing may be reordered (see prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness). Per-edge deletion sensitivity, from the harness: skip the payout and the allowance moves 206.10 -> 335.00; skip the fee and the settlement moves 87.80 -> 64.30; skip the settlement and the period containing the incident day stays unpaid, so the payout may not be released at all and the terminal state differs by the payment entry and by premium_outstanding (62.47 instead of -25.33). user_scenario mentions no prerequisite problem (prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint) and no tool validates one (prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block).
5. THE BASE-INVARIANT CARD (per exact write subject, at handling time)
   protection_premium_charge (the fee) and protection_premium_payment (the settlement) are governed by protection_premium_billing, whose only gate is billable_plan_state: 'Premium is billed, and premium payments applied, only while the plan stands in application_received, active or claim_hold.' Authority system_record, timing pre_action, correlation key protection_plans.plan_id bound to the plan_id argument. The plan stands active in the seed, so both hold. protection_combo_membership_interaction governs the charge as well and carries no structured gate; its scope is inherited as policy_scope (the tier discount is read as it stands on the day the premium is billed - here Circle Plus Annual, active, five percent).
   protection_claim_payout (the payout and the allowance) is governed by protection_claim_settlement (payable_plan_state: 'A payout is booked only while the plan stands active or in claim_hold' - the plan is active), protection_agg_payout_cap (its cap clause is now superseded clause by clause in both payout policies and implemented: the room the cap leaves is the plan's 12000.00 aggregate cap less the payouts booked on the plan in the rolling twelve months, and the cut-back is applied after the per-claim limit and the cover left, never before them, as base requires. The profile holds one plan; the twelve-month total of payouts is 5030.00 before this call, 6278.90 when the allowance is worked out and 6485.00 after both writes, so the room is 6970.00 against a write of 1248.90 and 5721.10 against a write of 206.10 and the cap never binds - but it is now a binding of both computes rather than a dropped branch), protection_combo_membership_interaction (no gate; the membership adds nothing to a covered repair) and protection_excl_duplicate_coverage, whose no_overlapping_warranty_settlement gate this difficulty retires by a declared overwrite in the repair-settlement policy and replaces with a sentence reading the same exclusion off the repairer's ledger; the manufacturer's warranty on a major appliance runs twelve months from 2025-11-08 and expired on 2026-11-07 - it has NOT expired, so the exclusion has to be faced squarely: the entries the plan meets are the ones the repairer booked as chargeable to the plan rather than to the manufacturer, which is exactly what the seeded job records (warranty_work_flag False on the TechWorks job, so no entry on it was warranty work).
   Time gates: none of the four writes is governed by a base eligibility of kind time (item_age_inside_limit governs protection_plan_purchase, report_window_open governs protection_claim_file, free_look_open governs protection_plan_cancel, review_days_not_exceeded governs protection_claim_hold_release and premium_grace_run governs protection_plan_terminate_nonpayment - all five of the base time eligibilities, and none of the five write subjects is one this task writes), so temporal_feasibility is deliberately empty. The two clocks that do bite are checked by hand: the claim report window (thirty calendar days from the incident day, day zero inclusive, anchored on protection_events.incident_date) was met - the failure of 2026-08-30 was reported on 2026-09-02, day three; it would just fail at a report on 2026-09-30 (day thirty-one) and just hold at 2026-09-29 (day thirty). The premium grace clock (thirty calendar days from the first day of the unpaid period, day zero inclusive) has run on three of the four unpaid periods: 2026-06-08 ran out on 2026-07-08, 2026-07-08 on 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-08 on 2026-09-07, while 2026-09-08 is only seven days old and has not. That boundary is what the periods counted toward the fee turn on, and it is why three periods carry the fee and not four.
6. THE BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
   Target object: the one ShieldCare Major Appliance Extended Service plan on the profile, initial_state.protection_plans.d9cb7845-045b-4398-b837-b71f554aa281, covering serial NBRF7734-2291447. Correlation keys: plan_id for every premium and cover row, claim_reference for every claim row, covered_item_serial for the item. The claim being settled is SC-2026-88413 and no other: the two earlier claims, SC-2026-10744 and SC-2026-31905, each already carry a decision, a payout and a settled deductible, so neither can be mistaken for an open one. Rows that enter each aggregate: the eleven monthly_instalment charges and seven payments (the arrears), the single late-fee row this call creates (the fees taken), the coverage grant of 6500.00 and the four payouts (the cover left), the three deductible charges and three payments (nothing unsettled), the claim file and decision rows of SC-2026-88413 (the incident, report and decision days). Rows excluded and why: the April allowance of 350.00 is the only payout of the reimbursement kind, which is what makes 'an allowance already paid out as money to the customer' identifiable; the January labour of 210.00 and parts of 155.00 sit on a different TechWorks job, on the television, and fall outside the six-month window read. Existing settlements: each of the three deductibles of 75.00 is matched to its own claim reference by a payment carrying that reference, so no deductible stands unsettled. The payout and the allowance both carry claim_reference and covered_item_serial into the new rows, so the derived entries are tied to the source claim and item rather than to the customer alone.
7. WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS (and what changes if it is removed)
   customers: the profile the call is about; its phone and card last four are the two credentials the verification tool needs. membership_holdings: Circle Plus Annual, active since 2019-03-06 - remove it and the fee for each unpaid period falls back to the plan's twelve dollars and the period taken ahead loses its five percent, moving the fee 23.50 -> 38.50 and the settlement 87.80 -> higher. protection_plans: the holding itself; its recorded premium_outstanding of 38.97 is DELIBERATELY STALE by one instalment (the 2026-09-08 charge) against the 51.96 the ledger carries. db_schema.json states that field as an identity - 'premium billed and not yet settled, identically the sum of the premium_receivable account deltas' - and this world breaks that identity on this one field by design, which is the stale-cache exception the authoring contract allows for a history task and which is declared here and in seed_consistency for the plan row; coverage_remaining (1470.00) and deductible_outstanding (0.00) both satisfy their own identities. Tier 1 of arrears_measurement_basis is reachable only on a world that breaks the identity, and that is the point of it: the policy alone settles which figure is authoritative, because the tier's condition compares two quantities the agent can read with find_protection_events and find_protection_plans, so there is one answer and not two. That is the single cache discrepancy in this world, declared here, and it is what the arrears-measurement factor turns on (read the recorded figure and the settlement comes out 98.31 instead of 87.80). The eleven instalment charges and seven payments: remove any one and the arrears, the unpaid periods and therefore the fee and the settlement all move. The coverage grant and the four payouts: remove one and the cover left moves, which moves the write-off on the fee and the ceiling on the allowance. The April allowance of 350.00: it is the 'allowance already paid as money' that puts the ceiling on the tier that reads the cover left; remove it and the ceiling becomes half the spoilage cover. The three deductible charges and payments: they are what make the household excess fifteen dollars rather than thirty. The claim file and decision rows of SC-2026-88413: the incident day (2026-08-30), the report day (2026-09-02) and the decision day (2026-09-08) drive the outage clock, the promptness share and the write-off. The two TechWorks jobs and their seven entries: the repairer's bill the payout is built from, plus the near-miss pair in January that a twelve-month window would wrongly include. The three claim intakes: they show the statement signed and the proof of purchase received, which is what lets an approved claim be settled at all.
   Automatic-clause check: the plan reinstates its cover at each anniversary, and the first anniversary (2026-12-08) has not arrived, so no reinstatement is due and no zero-delta row was seeded. Expiry is 2030 away. Termination for non-payment is deliberate negative space: grace on three periods has run, so the retailer COULD have ended the plan, but base provides that where the customer settles everything outstanding on or before the day of termination the plan is left in force and the termination is not booked - which is what happens on this call. No tool of this difficulty can terminate a plan, so the agent cannot be drawn into it.
8. THE PERSONA (design)
   Delia Harkness is a piano teacher with a three-times-failed refrigerator; her voice is patient and a little worn, and the text is organised the way she would actually talk - the grievance and the request first, then what she will only give when asked, then how she reacts. Volunteered at the opening: the three failures, the thawed freezer, the claim number on an envelope, and one clear request - the food she lost out of the freezer, covered, today if it can be - plus the authorisation boundary (the desk may act on the plan for her; she will put through herself anything handed to her). Given only when asked: the mobile 3124470186, the card last four 2318, the postal code 60614, the serial she reads off the sticker inside the door, the two dates, and the answer that no other cover has met the spoiled food. Reacted to only after the representative says something: the premium being behind (she blames a lapsed card, then pays what she is told, on the card the plan is billed to), the repair being settled with the engineers, and the allowance being paid (she thanks them, mentions store credit, and the call ends there - exactly where evaluation_criteria ends). The natural trap is the stale account page: she remembers something under forty dollars outstanding, which is the recorded 38.97, and if she is told a bigger figure she asks once for it to be checked against the bill without ever supplying a formula or a correct number. She never names a fee, a period past grace, an arrears, the repair payout or the cover left; she never asks for anything after the allowance; and she asks for no document to be sent anywhere, so nothing she says sits outside gold.
9. DEPTH AND BREADTH
   Depth (four hops, each entailed by a prerequisite sentence in the blocked policy's own rule): spoiled food -> the ceiling on the allowance waits on the approved cost standing paid -> the payout waits on the period containing the incident day being settled -> the settlement waits on the fee for the periods past grace standing billed. Nothing in that chain may be swapped. Breadth, per computation: the fee reads the premium ledger (eleven charges, seven payments), the claim decision history, the cover ledger and, across products, the Circle tier's plan discount and its activation day; the settlement reads the premium ledger twice over (the entries and the recorded figure - the cache trap), the fee rows, the claim decisions, the coverage end day and the membership again; the payout reads the TechWorks ledger on two jobs (labour, two parts lines, an attendance charge, a diagnosis, an included-visit count), the plan's repair tally, the item purchase day, the term length and the cover ledger; the allowance reads the cover ledger after the payout, the reimbursement history, the claim file and decision days, the service job's completion day and the deductible pairs. Negative space: no plan termination, no deductible on this claim (all three are already settled), no membership labour discount on covered work, and no second allowance for the April failure.
10. WHERE CARELESSNESS BITES, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES IT
   (a) Reading the plan's recorded premium outstanding (38.97, or 62.47 once the fee is on) instead of rebuilding the arrears from the entries: the settlement rule says which basis applies when the entries exceed the recorded figure, and the entries do. (b) Counting four unpaid periods toward the fee: the period beginning 2026-09-08 is seven days old against thirty grace days, and the rule counts only the periods whose grace has fully run. (c) Reading the repairer's bill over twelve months: that pulls in the January television job, and the rule reads six months where a diagnosis stands recorded and the plan is not a priority one. (d) Taking the plan's 350.00 spoilage cover as the ceiling: the rule takes the cover left once the cover has fallen below three tenths of the term limit and an allowance already stands paid as money, which it has. (e) Booking the allowance before the payout: the ceiling would then be 350.00 and the answer 335.00. (f) Paying the allowance for the full ceiling: the household excess of fifteen dollars bites because three claims stand decided inside twelve months. (g) Counting the days out of use to the decision day instead of the completion day recorded on the job: that gives nine days and a seventy percent share. (h) Stamping the fee entry with a period other than the oldest one standing unpaid: the rule names that day outright, and the periods the amount is worked out over do not move it. (i) Paying the repairer without the authorisation number the decision issued, or to a party the decision did not name: the rule pays the party the decision named against the number it issued, and only RA-2026-0903 and on_site_technician answer to that on this claim.
11. THE STANDARD SOLUTION AND THE EXECUTED RECALCULATION
   Read: the profile by the stated mobile; verify on two details; the plan; the whole protection ledger; the claim intakes; the membership; the two service jobs and their entries. Then write, in the order the prerequisite sentences entail: the fee (23.50, stamped with the oldest unpaid period, 2026-06-08), the customer's settlement (87.80, through the handover), the approved cost (1248.90, paid to the on-site technician the decision named against authorisation RA-2026-0903) and the allowance (206.10).
   Harness actually executed (scratch script; it imports the gate's own evaluator and the real tools, replays each write onto the seeded DB and evaluates each policy on the world standing just before its own write):
     protection_ext_premium_late_fee_scale: result=23.5 (bindings 17, branches 13, history rows 23); factor baselines 38.5 / 33.5 / 17.5 / 30.0; all-baseline 48.0
     protection_ext_premium_arrears_settlement: result=87.8 (25, 17, 20); 98.31 / 64.3 / 64.3 / 75.46 / 88.45; all-baseline 62.47
     protection_ext_claim_repair_settlement: result=1248.9 (23, 21, 7); 1470.0 / 697.74 / 1119.75 / 1159.9 / 1210.4; all-baseline 721.95
     protection_ext_spoilage_allowance: result=206.1 (20, 14, 17); 335.0 / 139.77 / 73.44 / 161.88 / 191.1; all-baseline 82.0
     prerequisite sensitivity: allowance without the payout 335.0; settlement without the fee 64.3
   Those figures are exactly the expected values, the baseline_result values and the factor_sensitivity entries recorded in computations, and check_compute recomputes every one of them at handling time.
12. RULE <-> COMPUTE TWO-WAY SWEEP (per policy)
   Forward: every binding that reads the world, aggregates, chooses, crosses a category, caps or rounds carries a verbatim quotation of the rule sentence it implements in compute_basis - 60 entries across the four policies, one per binding, with each ladder binding quoting the whole tier sentence so every tier's condition and value is on the page. Reverse: every load-bearing sentence of each rule is claimed by a binding. Late fee: arrears sentence -> instalments_billed/instalments_paid/arrears_amount; whole-periods sentence -> unpaid_periods; fee ladder -> member_plan_discount/member_years/fee_per_period; periods-counted ladder -> payments_12m/newest_period_start/days_since_newest_period/chargeable_periods; rate ladder -> prior_fees_12m/escalation_pct; write-off ladder -> decisions_3m/cover_left/write_off; the product sentence -> result. Settlement: the four baseline sentences -> recorded_arrears/fees_taken/advance_periods/result; the measurement ladder -> charges_all/arrears_measure; the past-grace sentence -> newest_period_start/days_since_newest_period/periods_past_grace; the fees ladder -> fees_in_year/latest_fee_amount/payments_12m/fees_taken; the share ladder -> unpaid_periods_count/fee_count_12m/fee_share_pct; the periods-ahead ladder -> decisions_3m/months_of_cover_left/advance_periods; the discount ladder -> member_plan_discount/member_grace_discount/advance_discount_pct. Payout: the window ladder -> diagnoses_recorded/priority_handling/bill_window_months; the parts-met ladder -> parts_entries/largest_part/latest_part/latest_diagnosis/parts_base; the three share ladders -> their own bindings; the cover sentence -> coverage_credited/payouts_booked/cover_left; the ceiling sentence -> claim_ceiling; the lower-of sentence -> result. Allowance: the cover sentence -> coverage_credited/payouts_booked/cover_left; the ceiling ladder -> prior_allowances_12m/allowance_ceiling; the clock ladder -> work_completed_date/diagnoses_on_job/days_out_of_use; the two share ladders and the excess ladder -> their own bindings; the product sentence -> result. Sensitive words cross-checked: every quotation naming 'the last twelve months', 'the last three months', 'the window read' or 'inside that time' has a within_months on its expression; every 'no more than' or 'whichever is the lower' has an MN; every 'taken to the cent' has an RND; every 'never below nothing' has an MX; every 'where ... and ...' has a ternary whose test combines the two reads.
   Declared overwrites, scoped clause by clause. The late-fee policy declares two on protection_premium_delinquency, because the one base sentence carried two provisions: 'The plan's late fee is billed once' is superseded by the amount sentence (base gives the plan's 12.00 late fee once, the extended fee is 8.00 for each of three periods at one hundred and twenty-five percent less 6.50, that is 23.50), and 'when grace runs out' is superseded by the period sentence, 'The fee is billed against the first day of the oldest premium period standing unpaid on the plan, whichever later periods the fee is worked out over', which is what fixes the scored period of the entry. The rest of that base sentence - 'the premium already owed stays owed after termination' - is untouched and inherited. The payout policy declares two: protection_agg_payout_cap's cap clause, superseded by a sentence that measures the room on the payouts booked on this plan in the rolling twelve months (base aggregates across every plan the customer holds; the profile holds one, so the two agree here, but they part on a multi-plan profile, which is why it is declared) and implemented in cap_room; and protection_excl_duplicate_coverage's warranty bar, superseded by a job-level sentence and now implemented in warranty_job and warranty_exclusion - the covered item was bought 2025-11-08 and the repair entries are dated 2026-09-10, inside the twelve months a manufacturer's warranty ordinarily runs on a major appliance, so under the base bar the plan would pay nothing and under the extended rule it pays the covered bill of the job the repairer booked as work the warranty was not running to meet. Two declarations were withdrawn in this revision: the cap clause of protection_claim_settlement ('where the approved cost is above either cap...') was a restatement, not a conflict, so the declaration and the restating sentence are gone and base's cap behaviour is simply inherited; and protection_excl_duplicate_coverage's 'the customer is asked what has already been paid rather than being paid twice' is no longer retired, so the base reduction for cover a card issuer or household insurer has met keeps its stated means of discovery - the caller is asked, and answers ('she says no, nobody has and she has claimed nowhere else'). The spoilage policy declares one, protection_agg_payout_cap's cap clause, on the same footing and implemented in its own cap_room. Everything else is inherited: no base eligibility is weakened, the per-claim limit and the cover ceiling stand as base states them, the oldest-period-first allocation and the surplus rule stand, and the order in which the caps apply is base's own.

13. GATES RUN, AND THE CLOSURES
   check_extended --task 0: EXTENDED OK. check_task_tools: TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK. replay_tasks --task 0: REPLAY OK (16 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous, 0 errors, closure 49 = seeded 49). check_solvability --task 0: SOLVABILITY OK (4 calls, 9 base gates, 35 seed rows). check_compute --task 0: COMPUTE OK (4 computations, 19 factors, 6 cross-difficulty, 67 history rows, 65 branches). check_grounding --task 0: GROUNDING OK. check_cross_fire --task 0: SCOPE OK.
   Revision log. (i) Symptom: check_extended rejected the outage-share factor because none of its bindings read records. Root cause: its ladder read only a prior binding and a tier parameter. Change: the incident-date read was moved into that factor's own bindings. Re-run: EXTENDED OK. Propagated to the factor card in section 12 only (no figure moved). (ii) Symptom: replay_tasks reported closure 46 against 49 seeded rows. Root cause: the three claim intakes were never read by any action. Change: a find_protection_claim_intakes read was inserted as action 4, which is in any case what shows the statement signed before an approved claim is settled; every later action index, every computation step and every prior_step reference was bumped in the same pass. Re-run: REPLAY OK, and check_solvability / check_compute re-run green on the new indices. (iii) While laying the world out, the first draft had three repairs authorised before the August decision, which base would have settled by replacement rather than repair; the parts-share tier was restated as 'no more than the plan's repair attempts figure' and the seeded history reduced to two prior claims, so the seeded decision of approved_repair is exactly what the charter gives.
   Policy -> GT closure: each of the four policies computes one argument of one tool call - late_fee_amount at action 9, settlement_amount at 11, payout_amount at 13, allowance_amount at 15 - and charter_scope.extended_policies, required_documents and the computations' policy ids are the same four ids in the same order. Terminal state: one late-fee entry of 23.50 and premium_outstanding raised to 62.47; one premium payment of 87.80 and premium_outstanding at -25.33 (a surplus held against the period taken ahead, which base provides for); one payout of 1248.90 and cover at 221.10; one allowance of 206.10 and cover at 15.00. No other obligation of the seed is left unhandled.

Delia Harkness is fifty-eight, teaches piano out of a bungalow on the north side of Chicago, and has the sort of patience that comes from listening to scales all day. She is not cross, but she is tired of this refrigerator. It is the big Northbeam side-by-side she bought new last November, and it has now let her down three times: once in January, again in April, and then at the end of August, when it stopped cooling overnight and she came down in the morning to a freezer full of thawed meat and a puddle across the kitchen floor. The engineer has been out since, the fridge is running again, and she has the claim number written on the back of an envelope: SC-2026-88413.

What she wants out of this call she says plainly, almost as her first sentence: she wants the food she lost out of the freezer covered, today if it can be. She has no idea what the plan allows for spoiled food and will not pretend to; the paperwork, she says, is all Greek to her, and she would rather the desk worked it out and did whatever needs doing on her side of it, whatever that turns out to be. She is content for the representative to act on the plan for her, and she will put anything through herself if it is handed to her.

She volunteers little else. Her mobile is 3124470186 and she gives it when asked whose account this is; asked for something else that is on file she reads out the last four digits of the card the plan is billed to, 2318, and if she is pressed for one more thing she gives the postal code, 60614. She does not know any customer number and says so. Asked for the serial on the appliance she goes and reads it off the sticker inside the door and spells it out: NBRF7734-2291447. Asked when the fridge went, she says the last night of August; asked when she rang it in, she says the second of September, first thing in the morning. Asked whether anyone else has paid her for the spoiled food, a household policy or the like, she says no, nobody has and she has claimed nowhere else.

On money she is vague in the way real people are. If the representative tells her the premium on the plan has fallen behind she does not argue the point; she says she must have let the card lapse over the summer, that she had the account page showing something under forty dollars outstanding a while back and assumed the automatic payment had caught it. Once she is told a figure and handed the means to do it she will pay off whatever is behind on the plan there and then, on the card the plan is billed to. Should the figure she is told be bigger than the number she remembers from that page she says so once, that it is more than the account page was showing her and would they check it against the bill, and she takes the answer she is given without asking how it was arrived at.

She chases nothing she has not been told about. If the representative says the repair itself is being settled with the engineers, she says good, that is between them and the shop. If she is told the allowance for the spoiled food has been paid and is given a figure for it, she thanks them, says she will watch for it on her store credit, and for her the call is over. Anything the small print would answer she has no view on at all and leaves to the desk.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain, so no two problems may be reordered: the fee must stand billed before the settlement is measured (the settlement reads the fees standing on the plan inside the last twelve months), the settlement must land before the payout is released (the payout waits on the period covering the incident day being settled), and the payout must be booked before the allowance is worked out (the allowance ceiling is taken from the cover left). Each edge is stated by a prerequisite sentence in the rule of the problem it blocks, so the order is entailed by the policies and not by convention; there are no parallel edges to reorder.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The caller raises only the spoiled food: her opening request is that she wants the food she lost out of the freezer covered, and she says the plan's paperwork is all Greek to her. Nowhere does she mention a fee, a period past grace, an arrears, a repair payout or the cover left on the plan, and she drops no hint that something must be sorted out first. Every contribution she makes to the three prerequisite problems is a reaction to something the representative has already said: she pays what the plan is behind only once she is told the premium has fallen behind and is handed the means to pay, and she comments on the repair only if the representative says it is being settled with the engineers.
